name: Gateway of India
blurb: The basalt arch everyone walks past to get somewhere else. Twenty minutes is enough; an hour if you sit on the sea wall.
description: Built as a landing point for visitors from across the sea, and now the city's most-photographed arch. The plaza in front is wide, flat and open, so it works for a short stop with a toddler or a wheelchair. The colonnade on the water side shades benches in the afternoon.

__meta.note: Operational fields are demo estimates, not surveyed.

name: Taj Palace — Palace Kitchen
blurb: The one Colaba meal you budget most of the day for. Two hours minimum, so it only works if it is the plan.
description: A formal dining room inside a heritage hotel, so the room is the point as much as the food. Expect a long lunch rather than a quick stop: this does not fit a two-hour window with anything else in it. Book well ahead; walk-ins are a gamble.

__meta.note: Price and hours are demo placeholders for a real venue, not its published tariff. Verify before any public use.

name: Colaba Causeway — back lanes and shops
blurb: Cosmetic chains, book stalls, a good deal of noise. Side lanes behind the main drag are where the actual shopping is.
description: The main stretch is a corridor of chain stores and pharmacies; the side lanes a block back are small shops, a book stall and tailoring counters. Pavement is uneven and there are steps down into several units, so it is hard going with a stroller. Good for a browse, bad for a tight schedule.

name: Cafe Mondegar
blurb: An art deco building with a cafe on the ground floor and a courtyard behind it. Quietest good coffee in Colaba.
description: The room downstairs is small and gets loud quickly; the courtyard out the back is the better half. Sits people well for a working morning, less well for a quick in-and-out. Stairs to the upper floor, so the courtyard is the step-free route.

name: Cafe Bhaskara
blurb: South Indian filter coffee upstairs, art downstairs. Closed Mondays, which catches people out.
description: Two small rooms stacked over each other. The South Indian room is reached by a narrow staircase with a turn in it, so it is a difficult carry for a pram and impossible for a wheelchair. The art room below is flat and can be used without going up.

name: Bademeir Cafe
blurb: Bagels and a fifteen-minute stop. Small room, so it works when nothing else on the plan does.
description: Built for a quick stop rather than a sitting. Counter service, a handful of tables, and a menu that leans heavily on bagels and sandwiches. If your window is under half an hour this is the kind of place that still returns a stop.

name: K Supplies
blurb: All-day breakfast on a pavement-facing room. Reliable when the plan is already full and you still need a stop.
description: A narrow room with a few tables and a menu that runs all day rather than stopping at noon. Useful as the low-stakes stop between two heavier ones, because nobody expects you to stay.

name: Britannia & Co.
blurb: A Parsi-Iranian cafe that has outlasted most of its neighbours. Berry pulao, and a lot of regulars.
description: Wood-panelled, dim, and busy with people who have been coming for decades. The berry pulao is the thing to order. Long lunch or a late evening sitting; it is not a place you drop into for twenty minutes.

name: Leopold Cafe
blurb: Open late, reliably busy, and the easiest sit-down in Colaba if you have nothing else. Tourist-facing and unapologetic about it.
description: A large, loud, late-opening room in the middle of Colaba. Convenient rather than authentic: the food is broad and the crowd is a mix of everyone in the area. Useful as an easy stop in the evening when hours, not taste, are the constraint.

name: The Tulip — verandah tables
blurb: Shaded verandah tables that stay usable in light rain — the reason it is on this list at all.
description: Half the seating is on a covered verandah, which is what makes it a workable monsoon stop: you keep the outside table and lose the weather. Indoors is cooler but small.

name: Cafe Foyer
blurb: Brownie, coffee, a short bench of tables. A reliable half-hour stop off the Causeway.
description: Small, warm, and busiest at peak chocolate-drinking hours. Nothing to book and nothing to plan; it is the kind of stop that fills a gap between two longer things.

name: Royal Bombay Yacht Club
blurb: A private club behind a gate — the lawn, the sea view and the facade are the reward, and the terrace is the way in.
description: Not open to the general public for a walk-in, but non-member guests can buy a drink and use the sea-facing terrace. The grounds and building are worth seeing regardless. Fenced, level, and shaded; the hard part is the entry, not the ground.

__meta.note: Entry is for members and paying guests; the rest of the grounds is not public.

name: Causeway Frames Walk
blurb: A small photography walk that uses shop windows, doorways and a fire escape as its subject. Eight people per run.
description: Runs on a loop from the Causeway down to the Apollo Bandar edge, stopping four or five times to make one frame rather than twenty. A photographer walks ahead and talks about light on wet stone, so it is slower than it sounds. Not run in the monsoon.

__meta.note: Invented operator for the demo. The walk concept is real; the name and the schedule are not.

name: Mehfil at the Dhow Foyer
blurb: Twenty-four seats, one tabla player, a ghazal singer, and chai between sets. No amplification worth the name.
description: A first-floor room modelled on a dhow's cabin, with matting, low lighting and cushions. A ghazal is set, then the room talks, then the next set. Twenty-four people only, so it sells out. One flight of narrow stairs with no lift and a corridor you have to squeeze along.

__meta.note: Invented operator. Real small-room ghazal venues of this kind exist; this name and room are not real.

name: The Wada Room, Colaba
blurb: A restored wooden bungalow opened a few rooms at a time by a family trust. Entry is a caretaker, a donation box, and a locked door.
description: Original timber, a verandah with the sea on one side, and a caretaker who will talk about the house for as long as you let him. Donation, not ticket: pay what you think it is worth. The verandah is up two steps, and the interior is a single level once you are inside.

__meta.note: Invented property. Modelled on the small family-run wada houses that exist in the area.

name: Farsi Reading Room
blurb: Above a bookbinder's shop: eleven seats, Farsi papers, no sign. Hours are whatever the owner feels like.
description: Someone put a door through a wall, bought twelve chairs, and put out the newspapers. No sign, no website, no card machine. You read, you talk if you get talking, you leave when he closes up. The two steps into the shop are the only real barrier.

__meta.note: Invented. `hours.status` is deliberately unparsable so the hours adapter is exercised on a real record, not just in tests.

name: Kite Corner — paper and cane
blurb: Make a kite on a flat roof, then fly it off the same roof. Children leave with the thing they made.
description: Kite paper, split cane, string, and about forty minutes of measuring. The second half is flying, on a roof with a net, so there is a hard boundary. Works with a child from about six; younger children can cut and paste the tail while someone else flies.

name: Steps Sketch Hour
blurb: Life drawing on stone steps with charcoal, twenty poses, and a hard stop at noon.
description: A tutor, a board on the top step, and a model who holds each pose for two minutes. Charcoal only, so nothing to carry back except the drawing. The steps are uneven and the light is direct by eleven, which is why it stops then.

name: Colaba Lighthouse Point
blurb: The last point of land before the sea, with a working lighthouse and a fence around it. Half an hour is plenty.
description: A lighthouse, a rocky point, and the widest view of the harbour in Colaba without being in a crowd. Ground is broken and the fence has a gap that is technically not a gap. Nothing to do but look and take a photograph.

__meta.note: A Colaba-seaward lighthouse point exists; the exact position here is approximate and must be reconciled with the OSM snapshot.

name: Chaat Mile Marker
blurb: Four carts within thirty metres of each other. Seventeen hundred onwards, cash only, and standing up is how you eat it.
description: Not one stall but a cluster: aloo bhaji, misal pav, bhel, and a pani puri cart that works the evening crowd. Standing space on the pavement, nowhere to sit. The spice level is real and there is no non-spicy version, which is worth knowing before you commit.

name: Tiffin at the Wadi
blurb: Dabba carriers opening their tiffins at seven in the morning. Twelve rupees a plate and you are eating what the neighbourhood eats.
description: A row of dabba wallas, each with its own tiffin, working from seven until the boxes are empty — often by nine. Bhakri, phulka, one vegetable and one dal, no choice at all. Cash, plastic plates, and nowhere to sit; you stand on the pavement like everyone on that street.

__meta.note: Dabba wallas are real across Mumbai. This is a named demo location, not a surveyed one. `hours.status` is `absent` on purpose: never surveyed, so the engine must reject on `hours_unverified` rather than guess.

name: Stained Glass Bench
blurb: Two hours at a glazier's bench cutting, leading and setting a small panel. Six people, and you take the panel home.
description: The full sequence on a 20x30 cm panel: cartoon, cut glass, foiled, leaded, cemented, and a final polish. A working studio, so there is solder heat and noise, and a workbench that cannot be reached from a chair. No sitting out, no children.

name: Monsoon Film Walk
blurb: Six weeks a year this walk exists at all: reflections, umbrellas, and shop awnings. It is the one item in Colaba the rain improves.
description: A photographer leads a short loop looking for wet-street reflections and people under awnings, stopping under cover each time. Deliberately built so the plan does not have to abandon the street when the rain starts. Cancelled in a downpour; the leader phones you.

__meta.note: Keyword list deliberately avoids non-ASCII tokens; earlier revision carried one and it is worth keeping the tokeniser free of them until FTS indexing is verified.

name: Colaba Jazz Corner
blurb: Two sets of trio jazz in a basement, doors at nine, second set at half ten. Barely a phone signal in there.
description: A small basement bar with a piano, an upright bass, and a drum kit that is genuinely too loud at the second set. Two sets, then it stops. Eighteen covers and a door that most people queue for on a Wednesday, so book it. Four steps down to the door.

name: Old Dispensary Reading Room
blurb: The dispensary counter is still there, with a plywood table in front of it and a man who lets you sit.
description: Half preserved municipal dispensary, half sitting room: the dispensing counter, a faded queue-number board, and a plywood table. Entry through a lobby in an ordinary residential lane. He is there some mornings and not others.

name: Parsi Cafe Window Tables
blurb: Four tables under the window awning, a short menu, and the fastest service in the lane on a busy evening.
description: Small, bright, and run by a family that has been here for three generations. Pavak, salli par eedu, and a cream and jam soda worth the stop. The window tables are outside but covered, so they survive drizzle. No reservations, so a group of six will wait.

name: Colour Therapy Walk, Apollo Bandar
blurb: A short guided walk that ends in twenty minutes of doing nothing, which is the part people remember.
description: Starts at seven, walks the waterfront edge for half an hour in near-silence, then sits everyone on the wall for the rest. A wellness practitioner talks very little; it is closer to a group silence than a class. Cancelled when it rains.

name: Solar Cafe, Apollo Bandar
blurb: A converted bungalow facing the harbour, with a lawn, a shade sail, and a kitchen that is good rather than famous.
description: A low building, a lawn with tables on it, and a terrace that catches the sea breeze after four. Long, unhurried, and the kind of place that turns a two-hour window into one stop and no more. Shade sail covers about half the lawn; the other half is bright at noon.

activities: a long lunch on the grass
